_note: The sealed held-out corpus is not in every checkout (for example the team repository does not carry it). This file keeps its hashes so the seal can still be checked: README.md publishes the canonical hash, and where the file is present it must match. Tests that need the file skip cleanly when it is absent.

eval/dhanush_m1_holdout.jsonl._note: Dhanush Kankanala's Milestone 1 holdout set (10 attacks, 10 ordinary, his own JSONL format, MIT). Kept OUTSIDE this repository on purpose, so it is never in the tuning path; it is not ported to the tollgate case format and no rule in this repository was written from it. Recorded here at handoff (2026-10-30) so any later copy can be checked. Not unseen: its author wrote it, scored the keyword baseline on it once, and relabeled one case (HA01) before handoff.
eval/dhanush_m1_holdout.jsonl.location: outside the repository: data/holdout.jsonl in Dhanush Kankanala's Milestone 1 zip
eval/dhanush_m1_holdout.jsonl.canonical_form: the JSONL rows as one JSON list, sorted keys, no spaces, ASCII escapes (as app/evaluation.canonical_sha256)

eval/fresh_blind_corpus.json._note: Dhanush Kankanala's fresh blind set (22 cases, 24 messages including 2 setup steps), received 2026-11-08 from branch dhanush-fresh-blind (commit 2edef1b). Hashes recorded at intake, before any run. Not used for any rule, prompt or tuning decision. One live run on 2026-11-11 (eval/blind_run_2026-11-11_console.txt); the file is now carried in the public export. Format and overlap with the other sets were checked by hash and id only.
